rows.description:
SABER-TOOTHED CATS — AMERICA’S ICONIC ICE AGE PREDATOR

I'm a brand new channel — help me reach my first 1K subscribers by hitting that subscribe button! ✅

The saber-toothed cat is one of the most iconic prehistoric creatures in history — yet for over a century, our image of it came from bones alone. In 2020, a mummified cub frozen for 35,000 years in Siberia rewrote everything we thought we knew, revealing thick fur, muscular necks, and anatomy built for surgical strikes.

rows.title: 35,000-Year-Old Saber-Toothed Cub Found
rows.description:
Have you ever wondered what a baby saber-toothed cat would look like? Researchers in Russia recently found a 35,000 year old saber-toothed cub in melting Siberian permafrost! This kitten differed significantly from modern lion cubs in that it had an unusual muzzle with a big mouth and small ears, a large neck, longer front limbs, and darker fur. Overall, melting permafrost because of climate change is not good news, but it can reveal amazing specimens like this saber-toothed cub!

rows.title: Frozen Saber-Toothed Cat Mummy Found In Siberia!
rows.description:
For hundreds of years, ice mummies have been pulled from or fallen out of permafrost deposits across the arctic and subarctic. You may be familiar with the impressive mammoth mummies of Siberia, but several decades have revealed a distressingly growing list of ice-age animals which have helped to flesh out the world of Pleistocene Eurasia more than any bone could ever do. We’ve seen bears, wolf heads, cave lion cubs, and woolly rhino and elephant calves, but a holy grail has finally been found – an animal from the Pleistocene for which there are no known modern analogues – a saber-toothed cat, of sorts. Let’s take a gander at the frozen mummy of a Homotherium cub, quite possibly one of the most important ice age paleontological discoveries ever made.

A perfectly preserved saber-toothed tiger cub was recently discovered in the Siberian permafrost. Up until now, all the prehistoric animals (namely Woolly Mammoths, Woolly Rhinos, Pleistocene Wolves and Cave Lions) that have been found in permafrost are those with closely relatives still living on this earth. rows.title: Sabretooth Kitten found in Permafrost
rows.description:
For more than 35,000 years, this sabre-toothed kitten lay frozen in the Siberian permafrost.

The cub was discovered in 2020 near the Badyarikha River in Yakutia, northeastern Siberia. It belonged to Homotherium latidens, an extinct species of sabre-toothed cat, and was only around three weeks old when it died.

Its preservation is extraordinary. Dark brown fur still covers its body, while its whiskers, claws, paw pads and even the shape of its small ears and muzzle remain visible.

Only the head and front portion of the body survived, along with some separate bones from the rear, but this was enough to give scientists something they had never had before: a direct look at what Homotherium actually looked like.

Compared with a modern lion cub of the same age, it had a much thicker, more muscular neck, longer forelimbs, smaller ears and unusually broad paws.

For thousands of years, our image of sabre-toothed cats came almost entirely from bones. This tiny frozen cub finally preserved the animal itself.

#Paleontology #ancienthistory #permafrost #ancientdiscoveries #history

rows.title: Unique 32,000 Years Old Mummified Saber Tooth Cat Cub Found in Siberia Still Has Fur
tags: on the banks of the badyarikha river
rows.description:
In 2020, diggers searching for woolly mammoth tusks unearthed a sabertooth cub mummified in Siberian permafrost. 
However, study was published only in Novemeber 2024 and scientists shared their findings on a frozen, mummified sabre-toothed cub discovered in one of the coldest places on the planet.
A member of the species Homotherium latidens, the cub was discovered in the Republic of Sakha, on the banks of the Badyarikha Rive, in eastern Russia.
Carbon dating indicates that the specimen is over 30,000 years old, proving the cub lived during the Ice Age or Pleistocene epoch. 
The remains of the mummy consisted of its head, chest, and front legs and paws which are extremely well-preserved.
Still covered in fur, is a first-of-its-kind discovery and could reveal more about the ancient species.
The cub had longer hair on the back of its neck than on its legs, along with longer hair under its chin and around its mouth.
After analyzing its teeth, the research team believed that the cub was around three weeks old when it died.
This area of Siberia is home to other prehistoric finds, such as woolly mammoths and rhinos; however, according to the study, finding mummified big cats is rare.
Paleontologists are hopeful that this find could provide a plethora of information on saber-tooth cats.
According to the comparative data, it’s likely that the Badyarikha mummy would have had 12 pairs of ribs compared to the 13 pairs of ribs of a modern-day lion. 
Because the Badyarikha mummy’s front feet were so well preserved, the team could determine that the mummy had similar claws to those of P. leo. 
 “The study of the mummy of the Homotherium latidens cub made it possible for the first time to observe its fur, the shape of its muzzle, the shape and position of the auricle [ear], the morphology of the mouth opening and nasal planum,” wrote the authors in the study.
